answer: A network tomography protocol curbs Sybil attacks by triangulating an agent's physical coordinates. Synchronized landmark nodes act as an attestation lantern, emitting a timing pulse that agents must sign within bounded round-trip windows, anchoring locations into state roots as durable as cedar. An attacker incurs scarce physical network interfaces and geo-distributed hardware per identity. However, transient packet jitter and route flaps can spuriously disqualify honest agents.
